label: Cross-attention is necessary for proper image-text fusion
description:
Reading the early Flamingo paper, the natural conclusion is: 'cross-attention is the right way to combine modalities — it's what frontier multimodal models use'.

This was true in 2022. The 2023-2024 reality is messier.

Most open-source VLMs in production (LLaVA, Qwen-VL, InternVL, Idefics) use **token concatenation** — project image features to LLM token embedding space, concatenate with text tokens, feed into one transformer. The LLM's standard self-attention handles cross-modal interaction.

**Why concat won open-source**:

1. **Implementation simplicity**: bolt a vision encoder onto an existing LLM with minimal architectural changes. Cross-attention requires adding new layers + careful integration.

2. **Reuses LLM's apparatus**: self-attention is what the LLM was pretrained with. Image tokens flowing through the same machinery gets the LLM's full reasoning power for free.

3. **Easier to scale**: more compute → more layers → more capacity. Cross-attention adds dedicated layers; harder to scale.

4. **Empirical performance**: at the parameter counts open-source operates (1B-70B), token concat matches or beats Flamingo-style cross-attention.

**Where cross-attention re-emerges**:

- **Long-context multimodal**: many images interleaved with text. Token concat blows context budget; cross-attention separates streams.
- **Frozen-LLM scenarios**: when modifying the LLM is risky/expensive (regulatory, compute), cross-attention adds capability without touching the LLM.
- **Streaming / real-time**: image features computed once, accessed by all subsequent text. Token concat would re-process everything.

Frontier models (Gemini Pro, GPT-4V) likely use mixes — concat for standard input, cross-attention for additional modalities. Details often closed.

The takeaway: there's no single 'right' fusion architecture. **Token concat for early fusion** is the practical default for most open-source. Cross-attention has specific use cases. Match to your task.
probeQuestions: Why do most open-source VLMs use token concatenation rather than Flamingo-style cross-attention?
When does cross-attention re-emerge as the right choice?
correctionPromptTemplate: The learner thinks cross-attention is the canonical fusion method. Reframe: token concat is the modern open-source default. Cross-attention has specific use cases (long context, frozen LLM, streaming). The 'right' choice depends on the task. Ask first — 'when you say cross-attention, what specific advantage are you reaching for?'
